abstract: A shared balloon flight over the Teotihuacán valley from Viaja Teotihuacan, sold as a flight-only fare or as a package with hotel transport, cave breakfast and a cooperative visit. It suits first-timers who want the most reviewed listing we cover.
description:
Experience an unforgettable adventure with Mexico's #1 hot air balloon company. With over 20 years of experience and the trust of more than 100,000 travelers, we are the BEST SELLER on this platform.

Our pilots, with both private and commercial licenses, operate new and colorful balloons, certified by the AFAC (Federal Civil Aviation Agency), guaranteeing safety and quality service.

fullDescription:
This Viator listing from Viaja Teotihuacan holds a 4.9 rating from 8,158 reviews, the most of any flight we review. It sells two options. On dates we checked in late October 2026 the flight alone cost about $148 per person, and the package with Mexico City transport and cave breakfast cost about $236. The operator calls itself Mexico's number one balloon company, which we cannot verify, so treat the review count as the stronger signal.

The flight-only option has you drive to the balloon port yourself, and the listing says it includes no breakfast. The operator messages you the exact Google Maps location and your arrival time the day before, and describes the port as five minutes from the Pemex Pirámides gas station. The package adds round-trip hotel transport, coffee and tea, bottled water, a flight of about 45 minutes, a sparkling-wine toast, a flight certificate, breakfast in a natural cave and a visit to a cooperative for an explanation of obsidian and maguey with a liquor tasting. The listing's duration runs from 2 to 8 hours, and that range is the gap between the two options.

Book the $148 fare if you have a car or are sleeping near San Martín de las Pirámides and want the rest of the morning to yourself. Book the $236 package if you are staying in Mexico City, because the pre-dawn drive is the main thing the extra $88 removes. One recent reviewer found the breakfast hurried and missed the show that was running there, so do not plan the package around a long sit-down meal.

Check the exclusions before you pay. Admission to the archaeological zone is not included in either option (INAH lists MX$210, about $11), and neither is a guide inside the ruins, photo and video packages or tips. Passengers over 100 kg pay MX$35 per extra kilo on the day, which is under $2. Like every flight here, this one depends on weather and wind, and the listing does not promise a route over the pyramids.

fullDescription:
This Viator listing from Volare holds a 4.8 rating from 4,438 reviews. It has three options. On dates we checked in late October 2026 the flight with no transport cost about $159 per person, round-trip transport from Mexico City cost about $186, and the transport option with extra time at the Teotihuacán pyramids was also listed at about $186. The operator says it has more than 15 years in the business and that the tour won a Top 10 Adrenaline Rush ranking from Viator; we have not verified either claim.

What differs from most listings here is the breakfast. The description says a Mexican breakfast is served at the balloon port after the flight, not in a cave, and the option text puts the total at 3 hours without transport and 6 hours with it. The flight is 30 to 50 minutes in a shared basket, with a coffee break before and a toast and diploma on landing. The operator flies once a day. Reviewers mention a mariachi band, a smooth flow from start to finish, and that the pyramid time felt rushed to one 4-star reviewer who was given a set time to explore.

Choose the $159 fare if you can drive to the Volare balloon port. Choose $186 for round-trip transport if you are staying in Mexico City; at a gap of about $27 it is one of the smallest transport premiums among the flights we cover. If you want to see the ruins at all, the extra-time version at the same listed price is the better pick, but confirm the price when you pick your date. Ruins admission is MX$210 (about $11) in cash at the gate, and no guide is included.

The listing sets a maximum of 120 kg per person, bars children under 5, and notes the flight depends entirely on the weather. It also says the direction and speed depend on the wind, so there is sometimes no flight over the archaeological site. It lists the experience as wheelchair accessible, which sits oddly with climbing into a basket, so ask Volare directly if that matters to you.

fullDescription:
This Viator listing from Visita Teotihuacan Mexico holds a 4.9 rating from 2,849 reviews and has two options. On dates we checked in late October 2026 the flight only cost about $154 per person, and the all-inclusive package cost about $231. The flight-only option lasts about 2 hours from arrival and includes a cookie-and-coffee break, a flight certificate and a sparkling-wine toast. The package runs about 7 hours and adds round-trip transport from Mexico City, a cave breakfast and 1.5 hours free at the pyramids, plus an explanation of the region and a liquor tasting.

The listing is more specific about the meal than most. The package breakfast is described as seasonal water, fruit, coffee, artisan bread, and chilaquiles with chicken, steak or egg, or an omelet, with vegan options available. If you pick the flight-only fare you must reach the operator's offices in Teotihuacán yourself; you can find them on Google as Gran Vuelo Teotihuacan, and the details are sent the day before. The operator says it has a wide pickup area in Mexico City and asks you to write if your location does not appear.

Choose the $154 fare if you have a car and want your own plans after landing. Choose the $231 package if you are staying in Mexico City and want the breakfast and a set block of ruins time. Reviewers like the Airbnb and hotel pickup and the friendly staff, but one 4-star reviewer found a basket crowded with five people on a side, and another said the balloon does not actually fly over the pyramids. A reviewer also suggests a hat or jacket for the cave breakfast.

Entrance fees, a professional photo and video package and any weight surcharge are not included; the operator charges MX$35 per extra kilo above 100 kg (under $2). The operator says it holds the AFAC documentation it needs and that its pilots have more than 15 years of experience, which are its own statements. The flight is weather-dependent and the pyramids cannot be promised from the air.

abstract: Excellentravel packages a shared balloon flight with a restaurant breakfast and a guided visit of the Teotihuacán zone, admission included, with private or shared transport. It suits travelers who want one hotel-to-hotel day with a guide.
description:
Fly over Teotihuacán in a hot air balloon for approximately 50 minutes and enjoy breathtaking views of the Pyramid of the Sun and the Pyramid of the Moon. (Sunrise visibility is subject to weather conditions).

For your comfort and safety, your driver and guide will pick you up from the lobby of your accommodation in a private vehicle.

Upon arrival, enjoy coffee and cookies while watching the balloon inflation process—a perfect moment for photos.

Continue with a guided visit of approximately 2 hours and 30 minutes to the archaeological site of Teotihuacan, where you will discover its history and culture.

fullDescription: This Excellentravel listing on Viator is a ground-and-air day built around a shared balloon flight. Two options are on the schedule. The shared-transport option is about $247 per person (MXN 4,500) on dates we checked in late October 2026. The private-transport option is about $357 per person (MXN 6,500) and gives you a private vehicle and a private guided visit. In both, the balloon basket is shared with other passengers in small groups, so private here means the van and the guide, not the flight. The listing's own description calls transport and the pyramids tour private, which fits the second option and not the first.

The morning, as the listing describes it: your driver and guide collect you from the lobby of your Mexico City accommodation, you reach the launch field for coffee and cookies while the balloon inflates, and you fly for about 40 to 50 minutes depending on weather and landing conditions. After the toast and flight certificate there is breakfast at a local restaurant, which is not the cave restaurant that several other listings feature. Then comes a guided visit of about 2 hours 30 minutes in the archaeological zone with an English and Spanish guide certified by SECTUR. The listing puts your return to the accommodation at about 1:00 pm. Zone admission is included, which saves the box-office fee of MX$210 for foreign visitors.

Choose the shared-transport option if you want a guide and an organized transfer and are happy to share the vehicle. The $110 gap to the private option buys the car and the walk to yourselves, which matters most for families, mixed-pace groups and anyone who wants to linger at a stop or skip one.

The flight follows the wind, and the listing itself says sunrise visibility depends on weather, so treat views of the Pyramids of the Sun and Moon as the plan and not a promise. Expect a pre-dawn pickup. One reviewer describes a 5 a.m. hotel pickup. The listing asks for at least a moderate level of fitness and is not recommended for spinal injuries, pregnancy or poor cardiovascular health. It states no weight rule, so ask before booking if you are over about 100 kg, since surcharges at that point are common among operators in the valley. The listing is rated 4.9 from 123 reviews.

description:
Embark on a one-day tour to take part in a hot air balloon ride over the Teotihuacan Pyramids! Select among the four available options, each one designed to perfectly trigger clients' needs! There are: balloon flight without transportation, balloon flight with breakfast and without transportation, balloon flight with breakfast and round transportation to the balloon port, and the most upgraded option, which includes round transportation and guided visits to the archeological site and Guadalupe Shrine.

Begin the day heading to the balloon port (whether on your own or in shared transportation, depending on the option you select) to begin the ascent up to the sky. Admire the panoramic views of the Pyramid of the Sun and the Moon, and be captivated by the beauty of the dawn's light upon the ancient city. Once landed, be part of a sparkling wine toast to celebrate the magic of the moment and be granted a flight certificate that will forever commemorate this unique day. Later, depending on your selected option, enjoy an included breakfast or use the free time to purchase breakfast at your own cost.

If a balloon flight over Teotihuacan is not enough, select the most upgraded option! After the balloon flight, meet a local guide to access the Archeological Site of Teotihuacan, and follow him around the place while listening to interesting insights about the history, architecture, and culture of this ancient civilization. Then, head to an obsidian workshop, learn about this volcanic rock and its use to create handicrafts, and participate in a tequila tasting to indulge in the flavors of traditional Mexico. Take the opportunity to try a traditional Mexican meal at a nearby restaurant (at your own cost).

Lastly, take the opportunity to enjoy also a guided visit to Guadalupe Shrine, one of the most important pilgrimage sites in the world. Learn about its historical background and its significance in Mexico and the religious panorama as well. Visit the Old Basilica, the New Basilica, and several chapels and monuments.

Summing up, this tour offers the perfect blend of adventure, culture, and history, promising an enriching and memorable experience. Select the option that best suits you and conclude your day with a deeper understanding and appreciation of Mexico’s rich heritage!

Pick the transport option if you are staying in Mexico City, since a reviewer calls it a must at that hour. Pick the full day only if you want the pyramids and a religious site in the same trip.
